result.description:
Position Summary
Training Officers work in a dynamic vocational, education and training environment in which they have to adapt and be responsive to changes in national curriculum, the VET Quality Framework, technological developments and a diversity and breadth of client training demands.

The role of the Training Officer embraces the extent of the learning process from program enquiry/advice through to assessing and determining the training requirements of clients, following onto managing the learning process for clients using a variety of training strategies including recognition of prior learning, recognition of current competencies, training delivery, workplace learning, delivery and assessment, formal assessment and reporting etc..  

The training Officer will have the vocational skills in the area that they are applying for with a minimum of three to five years’ experience in their chosen vocational area.

The Training Officer ideally would have at least have obtained the following competencies from the Training and Assessment Training Package or is able to demonstrate equivalent competencies. However if the candidate does not have these competencies or the full Training & Assessment Qualification they will agree to work with an accredited assessor until this qualification is achieved.

The Training Officer is expected to be innovative in responding effectively to the training demands of clients.  The Training Officer works in a wide variety of learning environments providing a range of flexible training and learning strategies to best meet the client needs including flexible delivery, workplace training and assessment, training room delivery, on line learning support etc.   

The Training Officer will be expected to be able to work effectively as a member of a team and be required to be involved in a range of course/program coordination and administration activities that support the effective operation of the company and the achievement of learning outcomes for participants.  

POSITION PARAMETERS
1.	SUPERVISION AND ACCOUNTABILITY The position reports to the Manager and may work in a number of program areas. 
2.	LOCATION Training Staff are required to work on site or at a designated training facility.  
3.	PARTICIPATION ON COMMITTEES Training Officers are required to attend program meetings and team meetings, or other external committees as required.

Duty Statement
1.	Develop and manage the learning process for participants. 
2.	Train in a range of subjects and programs in a variety of learning modes at locations specified by the Manager. (See Attachment 1 for position details)
3.	Prepare quality learning and assessment resources within the context of established curriculum, training packages under the national framework, competency standards, the diversity of students and client’s requirements. Unless otherwise agreed with the Training Officer, Intellectual Property in all material developed or produced shall remain within Industry Training & Workplace Services.
4.	Participate as a member of a team on a range of tasks including curriculum and program development, program delivery, professional development, marketing activities and administrative and operational functions.
5.	Undertake, where required, course coordination and a range of planning tasks relevant to the delivery of quality courses.
6.	Provide support and advice to participants of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities and implement appropriate support strategies and/or learning programs and strategies as required.
7.	Undertake as required a range of participant support service tasks to ensure the effective operation of the Company, for example participant selection, course advice, enrolment and telephone enquiry support.
8.	Research, adapt and develop innovative learning practices and delivery options that enhance the Company's capacity to meet the demands of participants. 
9.	Manage the delivery of training services to industry, including workplace visits, assessing training needs, developing training plans and coordinating the effective delivery of programs.
10.	Participate in and contribute to the development and implementation of evaluation and continuous improvement processes across the Company.
11.	Undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional and vocational competencies as a Training Officer.
12.	Comply with the quality assurance requirements of the Australian Quality Training Framework and the company’s Quality System.

SELECTION CRITERIA 
Qualifications
1.	The minimum training qualification is the Certificate IV in Training & Assessment or equivalent. 
2.	It is mandatory to have relevant vocational competence at or higher than the level being delivered or assessed through having qualifications and/or relevant industry experience. 
3.	Training Officers who do not hold the minimum or equivalent training qualification must undertake professional development to gain the training qualification within 12 months of commencement. In the interim, the training officer must agree to be mentored by a qualified Trainer who does hold the minimum or equivalent qualification

Training Excellence
1.	Demonstrated excellence in training, management of learning and assessment.
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to development of learning resources.
3.	 An understanding of current developments and innovative approaches in training.
4.	Demonstrated experience, or ability to, develop and conduct training programs suitable to the needs of industry.
5.	Demonstrated record of innovation in training and proven commitment to undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional competence.

Communication Skills
1.	Proven ability to operate effectively as a member of a team.
2.	High level interpersonal and communication skills.
3.	Demonstrated ability to provide support and advice to students of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities.
Administration
1.	High level organisational skills
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to the overall functioning of the company including record keeping, course maintenance and quality improvement and ability to use all relevant technology.

Further Information
For further information please contact Toni Hoyle.
Telephone 90227100 or 0419 908 425

Boston Scientific
Clinical Specialist - Electrophysiology
Queensland
$85,000+

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our elite sales team is made up of passionate, dedicated professionals, delivering the most advanced medical technologies to patients in need. By collaborating extensively with leading healthcare professionals you’ll see first-hand the impact you have on individual lives - one patient at a time. 

The position of Clinical Specialist, Electrophysiology (EP), provides field/remote clinical, technical & educational support in EP to assigned accounts across ANZ. The primary focus is to support new therapy introduction of Pulsed Field Ablation through our recent launch of the FARAPULSE™ system, demonstrating clinical expertise to influence superior outcomes. Frequent travel will be required as part of the role. 

The Clinical Specialist – Electrophysiology role is based in Queensland and reports to the Field Clinical Specialist Manager.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

•	Utilising your technical knowledge of:
o	The field of electrophysiology (including propagation of electrical circuits within cardiac tissue and the pathophysiology of electrical rhythm disorders), biophysics of radiofrequency, cryo-thermal ablation, 2D and 3D electroanatomical mapping principles to provide:
?	Clinical support including basic trouble-shooting, and clinical guidance to diagnose and treat cardiac arrhythmias
?	Provide the measurement of electrical circuits within the heart and perform stimulation protocols as per physician requests to measure the electrical conductivity of the heart to aid in the diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmias
?	Develop a deep technical understanding of, and provide the technical training of company products to Cardiac Electrophysiologists, Cardiac Physiologists and Nurses
•	Travelling as required to meet customer demand for the services described above.
•	Attending cases face to face (or remotely) with customers, operating Boston Scientific products where appropriate, and providing detailed training / advice to physicians on clinical attributes / techniques associated with Boston Scientific electrophysiology products including:
o	Providing clinical support for: FARAPULSE™, OPAL™, RHYTHMIA™, LAB SYSTEM PRO™, MAESTRO 4000™, METRIQ™, plus support for the full range of Boston Scientific EP Catheters
•	Developing deep understanding on the workflows and specificities of each hospital & business relationships with hospital personnel (e.g., through informal conversation, meetings, participation in conferences) to make new contacts in other departments within hospital and all stakeholders to ensure that products are trained and utilised in accordance with the Directions for Use.
•	Ensuring timely collection, reporting of all required medical documentation pertaining to our procedural device operation.
•	Responding to complex customer needs and complaints regarding products and service by developing creative and feasible solutions or working with other related personnel (e.g., sales, clinical, research, marketing, technical support) to develop optimal solutions.
•	Recording customer information and activities in company’s CRM system: use the system as an alignment tool with other commercial roles.
•	Completion of relevant administration including reporting, stock validations and inventory management
•	Attending meetings, conferences and exhibitions as required to promote Boston Scientific products and services.
•	Being available to support the broader ANZ Rhythm Management business on an as-needs basis

KEY COMPETENCIES REQUIRED FOR SUCCESS 

Product/Technical Knowledge
•	Successfully completes all relevant Electrophysiology training. 
•	Develop in depth knowledge of Electrophysiology procedure, products and treatment applications.
•	Proactively keeps up to date with technical knowledge in Electrophysiology.

Relationship Building 
•	Builds and maintains effective networks that add value in achieving work related goals.
•	Skilled in building rapport with a wide variety of individuals.
•	Understands the balance between taking time to build rapport and achieving objectives set.
•	Works effectively and collaboratively within the team environment.

Adaptability 

•	Responds resourcefully, flexibly, and positively when faced with new challenges and demands. 
•	Moves forward productively and optimistically under conditions of change or uncertainty.

Organisation & Reporting
•	Maintains well organised materials, files, system and reports.
•	Plans and prioritises territory activity.
•	Makes sure all parts of a job are completed in full, within deadlines, including follow-up plans and documentation.

Results Focused
•	Demonstrates a growth mindset.
•	Measures own performance and seeks feedback for self-development
•	Demonstrates resilience and has a strong sense of urgency
•	Recognises and acts on opportunities.
•	Maintains a flexible approach to meet goals

YOUR EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

•	Clinical case experience within Electrophysiology / Cardiac Rhythm Management is highly regarded
•	Understanding of conventional Electrophysiology (EP), including EP signal interpretation, 3D Mapping, Cryoablation and Troubleshooting experience is highly regarded
•	Knowledge of Cardiac Electrophysiology principles, including Radiofrequency, Cryoablation, and Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA)
•	Tertiary qualifications in biomedical engineering, science or a related field 
•	Desired qualifications in IBHRE EP, IBHRE Pacing
•	Strong technical and clinical skills
•	Demonstrated expertise in building and maintaining strong relationships.
•	Proven ability to absorb complex technical information and apply this knowledge in the field.
•	Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
•	Excellent written & verbal communication.

WHY CHOOSE US?
 
•	Great Place To Work Certified in 2024 & 2025
•	Best Workplaces for Women in 2024 & 2025
•	Inclusive Employee Resource Groups
•	2 Wellbeing Days per year
•	Discounted health insurance
•	Ability to purchase additional Annual Leave
•	Employee Stock Purchase Plan

Remuneration: - 
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM28301

What you'll be doing

The primary purpose of the Senior Resident Medical Officer (SRMO) in Orthopaedics is to provide clinical care, under appropriate supervision, to patients requiring emergency medical services in a complex clinical environment. This position will provide experience in a critical care environment and have responsibilities and opportunities for autonomous practice commensurate with the level of experience of the incumbent.

Where you'll be working

The Wagga Wagga Health Service has undergone a $431 million redevelopment. It was delivered in three stages and completed in 2021. The health campus includes: 

- a 325 bed referral hospital called Wagga Wagga Base Hospital. Opened in 2017, it supports over 40,000 emergency presentations, 1,100 births and approximately 11,000 operations each year. 

- a 24 hour Emergency Department equipped with telehealth cameras to connect the team in Wagga Wagga with other specialists or GPs across the state through the Critical Care Advisory Service, ensuring you get the care you need.

- a purpose-built Health Services Hub which opened in 2021. The new facility, linked to the Wagga Wagga Base Hospital, offers a range of important services from a single site.The multi-storey building accommodates acute aged care inpatient beds, rehabilitation inpatient beds, an older person's mental inpatient unit, Hospital in the Home, expanded renal dialysis unit, expanded oral (dental) service, 60 clinic rooms and treatment spaces for allied health, outpatient, and community health services. There is also a Staff Hub and 30 staff meeting rooms of varying sizes with an electronic booking system and the latest presentation technology; a new lecture theatre and two nearby conference rooms, new clinical education and training spaces, including a simulation room and skills area and facilities for virtual training; a library, a dedicated Aboriginal meeting room and cultural courtyard; cafe; new multi-faith space; and facilitiies for corporate volunteers. There is also secure parking for fleet vehicles under the Health Services Hub. 

- a specialised Mental Health Unit, which opened in 2013, to provide a large modern and comfortable facility. Community mental health services are co-located on the campus in the new Health Services Hub.

Wagga Wagga Health Service provides services including critical care, medical, surgical, paediatric, obstetric, and rehabilitation care. We also provide mental health and community health services. We work with a team of specialists which include cardiovascular, gastroenterology, renal medicine, obstetrics, orthopaedics, psychiatry and paediatrics. There is also the provision of a full range of allied health and support services such as oral health, physiotheraphy, occupational therapy, sexual health and violence prevention and response services.

Location

Wagga Wagga is the largest regional city in NSW with an urban population of over 60,000 residents, nestled on the banks of the Murrumbidgee River.

Wagga Wagga offers a myriad of activities to enjoy, including a wonderful selection of restaurants, cafes, markets and wineries, galleries and museums. It has terrific gradens and recreational areas and caters to both the cultural and sporting enthusiasts.

There are extensive education options from early childhood through to tertiary; including public and private primary and secondary schools, the TAFE NSW Riverina Institute, Charles Sturt University, The University of NSW Rural Clinical School, and The University of Notre Dame - Rural clinical School.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered with the Medical Board of Australia.

Unconditional general registration or eligible for unconditional registration with AHPRA

Demonstrated ability to work independently in a supervised environment

Adept ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team with an understanding of the roles of the doctor and other members of the healthcare team

Adept written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively and respectfully with patients, family members and others members of the health care team

Adept good organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management

Evidence of continuing professional development and commitment to self-education

About the Role: 

Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is eager to recruit an Occupational Therapist to work in our dynamic, growing and supportive team, to help us deliver exceptional care to our community. 

The Occupational Therapist (AHP2) is accountable to the Senior Manager, Clinical Manager or Nurse Unit Manager (NUM) of the Northern Adelaide Geriatric Service for the provision assessment and treatment services for patients of NALHN which aims to optimise health outcomes. The incumbent will rotate through a series of clinical services.

The Occupational Therapist applies clinical experience, increasing clinical knowledge and professional competence to plan, implement and evaluate comprehensive and integrated services to the needs of clients of NALHN. The Occupational Therapist (AHP2) works under limited direct supervision clinical supervision and may provide direction and support to less experience therapists, allied health assistants and students.

The Occupational Therapist works collaboratively with the multi-disciplinary team and liaises directly with medical, nursing staff of NALHN and with other community agencies.

To be eligible for this position, you must have an Appropriate Degree or equivalent qualification which entitles registration as an Occupational Therapist with the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia.

About You: 

In this role you will have strong interpersonal and communication skills which will enable you to successfully problem solve, resolve conflicts and negotiate, including the ability to engage in difficult conversations, whilst building and maintaining relationships. An ability to effectively manage multiple, diverse and competing priorities and demonstrated resilience within a stressful and complex environment is essential to this role. 

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a passionate, highly driven, dedicated and progressive team. 

About Us: 

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management. 

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community. 

Our 300-plus Allied Health professionals play an integral role in multidisciplinary teams delivering outstanding care to patients across our acute, subacute and hospital avoidance services. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

At NALHN, we have a strong commitment to providing a clinically interesting professional experience, with structured and supportive education and professional development, and career progression pathways. 

Some feedback from current employees about working as Allied Health Professionals in NALHN includes: 

"My favourite part about working in NALHN is the close working relationships we have across Allied Health to optimise patient care." 

"I feel like I'm part of a growing and developing service." 

"I love the great team dynamic and the culture of learning and support." 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services: 

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services. 

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services. 

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care. 

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings. 

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites. 

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains. 

Benefits of working at NALHN: 

From salary packaging to flexible working arrangements, a large range of opportunities for movement and career progression, you'll find there are lots of benefits of working with Northern Adelaide Local Health Network. 

Incremental wage increases in-line with the Allied Health Professionals, Assistants and Psychologists Enterprise Agreement 2025 

Access to experienced clinicians across a broad range of expertise, who are supportive of collegial sharing of skills and knowledge in different therapies and client presentations. 

Salary packaging is an option for saving money by paying for some of your everyday expenses from your salary before it is taxed. 

Relocation assistance may be available for successful applicants from interstate or overseas. 

NALHN supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions. 

In addition to this, other benefits of working as a Occupational Therapist in NALHN include: 

professional development opportunities. We have a well-established Allied Health Education unit which offers high-quality, targeted in-house training, and under the current enterprise agreement staff are also eligible for a Professional Development Allowance and entitled to claim reimbursement of eligible professional development expenses to allow you to continue to build upon your professional foundations 

opportunities to participate in research. NALHN have an Allied Health Research Chair, who is able to work with clinicians and teams to support clinical research 

regular clinical supervision, allowing you to receive individualised support, learning and development to help you achieve your career goals
